page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 96 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARM64 architecture (ARMv9 Neoverse-V2) running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The processor includes a cache hierarchy of 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 36 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 300 Gbps, managed via the Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8gn.24xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests place the instance in the top 10% of tested hardware, supported by its 96 dedicated physical cores with single-thread-per-core execution. Memory bandwidth is a primary strength, with cached read-only small block speeds reaching 11,078.02 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 242.04 GB/sec, both scoring in the top tier. Single-core performance, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, falls into the average range. Cryptographic operations are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, though other advanced vector and matrix extensions are absent.

Given its high memory-to-CPU ratio and exceptional memory bandwidth, the r8gn.24xlarge is highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that scale across many cores without requiring local NVMe storage. Top-tier performance in Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations (reaching 198.12 million operations per second) makes it highly suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, and data-intensive web serving. Additionally, strong multi-threaded decompression and top-tier software compilation performance make it fit for large-scale CI/CD pipelines, ETL processes, and medium-to-large LLM inference text generation tasks.
